Show the clustering at every k (see how it deteriorates)

Source: R/manuscript-viz.R
cluster_k_sweep.Rd

Rather than only reporting the best \(k\), project the objects to a fixed 2-D embedding and recolour them by the \(k\)-cut for each candidate \(k\) in a grid, annotating the average silhouette per panel. This makes it visible how the structure splits and degrades as \(k\) grows.

Usage

cluster_k_sweep(
  x,
  k_range = 2:6,
  linkage = "ward.D2",
  embed = c("pca", "umap", "tsne"),
  ncol = 3,
  point_size = 2.2,
  alpha = 0.9,
  palette = "Dark 3",
  base_size = 13
)

Arguments

x

A fitted result ($DistM), a dissimilarity, or a List.

k_range

Candidate cluster counts to display.

linkage

Agglomeration method used to cut the fused dissimilarity.

embed

Embedding for the (fixed) 2-D coordinates: "pca" (default), "umap" or "tsne".

ncol

Columns in the panel grid.

point_size

Diameter of the plotted points (default 2.2); raise it for larger, clearer markers.

alpha

Point opacity (default 0.9).

palette

Discrete hcl.colors palette used to colour the clusters (default "Dark 3").

base_size

Base font size passed to the ggplot2 theme.

Value

Invisibly the ggplot object (also printed, so it draws on an open device); the average silhouette per \(k\) is attached as the attribute "silhouette".

Details

The panels are drawn with ggplot2 for a clean, high-resolution result whose quality is preserved when the figure is rescaled – save the returned object to a vector device (PDF/SVG) or a high-DPI raster for publication, e.g. ggplot2::ggsave("ksweep.pdf", cluster_k_sweep(fit), width = 9, height = 6).

See also

cluster_selection_plot, embedding_plot

Examples

# \donttest{
data(mosaic_toy)
fit <- M_ABC(mosaic_toy$List, numsim = 40, NC = 3)
#> M_ABC: source 1 of 2 (weighting = var) ...
#> M_ABC: source 2 of 2 (weighting = var) ...
#> M_ABC: building consensus dissimilarity (C++ kernel) ...
cluster_k_sweep(fit, k_range = 2:6, point_size = 3)

# }
